body.question: Letters flash rapidly one after another and you must spot two targets, X and K. You catch the X. When is a second target K most likely to be missed?
options: About 200 to 500 milliseconds after the X
Only if K comes before the X
body.reveal: People struggle to notice a second target that appears 200 to 500 milliseconds after the first and is followed by distractions. This is the attentional blink. It is thought to come from a two-stage visual system: everything gets some processing, but only salient items get in-depth processing.

probes.question: True or false: the attentional blink means people can never see a second target in a fast stream.
In the stream B, X, C, K with targets X and K, which target is often missed?

image_brief.show: File:RSVP.png shows an example frame of a rapid serial visual presentation of letters

claims.claim: Second target is missed if it appears 200 to 500 ms after the first and is followed by distractions
claims.quote: struggle to notice a second visual target in a rapid sequence if it appears 200 to 500 milliseconds after the first

claims.claim: In a stream B, X, C, K with targets X and K, K is often missed (probe 2)
claims.quote: "K" is often missed if a letter like "C" comes between them

claims.claim: It does not mean people can never see a second target: they often fail, and consecutive targets are usually both noticed (probe 1)
claims.quote: people usually notice both because they are consecutive

claims.claim: Participants often fail to detect a second salient target within the blink
claims.quote: participants often fail to detect a second salient target if it is presented within the blink

claims.claim: Thought to come from a two-stage visual system
claims.quote: it is thought to be a product of a two-stage visual processing system

claims.claim: Everything gets some processing but only salient items get in-depth processing
claims.quote: all stimuli are processed to some extent by an initial parallel stage, and only salient ones are selected for in-depth processing
